'''Torus-based cryptography''' involves using [[Algebraic torus|algebraic tori]] to construct a [[Group (mathematics)|group]] for use in [[cipher]]s based on the [[discrete logarithm problem]]. This idea was first introduced by [[Alice Silverberg]] and [[Karl Rubin]] in 2003 in the form of a [[public key algorithm]] by the name of [[CEILIDH]]. It improves on conventional cryptosystems by representing some elements of large finite fields compactly and therefore transmitting fewer bits.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Rubin |first1=Karl |last2=Silverberg |first2=Alice |date=2003 |editor-last=Boneh |editor-first=Dan |chapter=Torus-Based Cryptography |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=2729 |title=Advances in Cryptology - CRYPTO 2003 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-45146-4_21 |language=en |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |pages=349–365 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-45146-4_21 |isbn=978-3-540-45146-4}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last=Gorla |first=Elisa |chapter=Torus-Based Cryptography |date=2025 |title=Encyclopedia of Cryptography, Security and Privacy |pages=2632–2634 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/rwe/10.1007/978-3-030-71522-9_481 |access-date=2026-02-03 |publisher=Springer, Cham |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-71522-9_481 |isbn=978-3-030-71522-9|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>
